title: Keep the debug dump working on Java 17

blocks.text: The support team's `/debug/dump` endpoint shows the instance fields of whatever object an engineer points it at. Since the service moved to Java 17, pointing it at a JDK object, such as the `ArrayBlockingQueue` behind the job scheduler, makes the endpoint answer 500, and the engineer gets nothing at all.

`FieldDump.dump(...)` already walks the fields. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/FieldDump.java`: `read(field, target)` returns the field's value as text, or `FieldDump.HIDDEN` when the JVM won't let the dump read it.

When you're done, the service's own objects show every field, private ones included; a JDK object shows whatever the JVM lets it read and `<hidden>` for the rest; and no object makes the dump fail. The tests run without any `--add-opens` option. About five lines.

cases.says: the service's own objects are dumped with every instance field, private ones included
a JDK object whose private fields the JVM won't open is dumped with every field hidden, and the dump doesn't fail
the public fields of a JDK class are read and shown; only its non-public ones are hidden

origin.section: Open One Package by Name, or Stop Reaching Inside

concepts: From Java 17, setAccessible(true) on a private member of a JDK package that is not opened throws InaccessibleObjectException, and trySetAccessible() returns false instead.
InaccessibleObjectException is unchecked and not a SecurityException, so reflective code that catches SecurityException and IllegalAccessException lets it through.
Strong encapsulation closes the private members of JDK packages; public members of exported packages stay reachable by reflection.
